# kea_dhcp4_client_class (Resource)

Manages a DHCPv4 client class in the Kea DHCP server. Client classes group clients by a test expression and assign options, boot parameters and lease lifetimes to them.

Kea evaluates client classes in the order they are defined, and `class-add` appends a new class at the end of the list. A class created by this resource is therefore evaluated after the classes from the configuration file and after the classes created before it. A class can only refer to classes defined before it, so use references or `depends_on` to create classes in the right order.

**Important:** Requires the `class_cmds` hook library. Kea keeps classes added through `class_cmds` in memory only.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Class matching a vendor class identifier
resource "kea_dhcp4_client_class" "voip" {
  name = "voip-phones"
  test = "substring(option[60].hex, 0, 6) == 'Aastra'"

  option_data {
    name = "tftp-server-name"
    data = "192.0.2.5"
  }
}

# PXE boot for UEFI clients
resource "kea_dhcp4_client_class" "pxe_uefi" {
  name           = "pxe-uefi"
  test           = "option[93].hex == 0x0007"
  next_server    = "192.0.2.5"
  boot_file_name = "grubx64.efi"
  valid_lifetime = 600
}

# Class with a custom option definition
resource "kea_dhcp4_client_class" "provisioning" {
  name = "provisioning"
  test = "option[60].text == 'provisioning'"

  option_def {
    name = "provisioning-url"
    code = 224
    type = "string"
  }

  option_data {
    name = "provisioning-url"
    data = "https://provisioning.example.com/"
  }
}

# Class only evaluated when a subnet or pool lists it in
# evaluate-additional-classes. Classes are evaluated in definition order,
# so depends_on keeps it after the classes it refers to.
resource "kea_dhcp4_client_class" "late" {
  name                    = "late-voip"
  test                    = "member('voip-phones')"
  only_in_additional_list = true

  option_data {
    name = "domain-name"
    data = "voip.example.com"
  }

  depends_on = [kea_dhcp4_client_class.voip]
}

# Template class spawning one subclass per client identifier prefix
resource "kea_dhcp4_client_class" "per_vendor" {
  name          = "per-vendor"
  template_test = "substring(option[61].hex, 0, 3)"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the client class.

### Optional

- `boot_file_name` (String) Boot file name for network booting (`file` field in DHCP packet, Option 67).
- `max_valid_lifetime` (Number) Maximum lease lifetime in seconds a client in this class can request.
- `min_valid_lifetime` (Number) Minimum lease lifetime in seconds a client in this class can request.
- `next_server` (String) Next server address for network booting (`siaddr` field in DHCP packet).
- `only_in_additional_list` (Boolean) When `true`, the class is only evaluated when a subnet, pool or shared network lists it in `evaluate-additional-classes`. Defaults to `false`.
- `option_data` (Block Set) DHCP options to send to clients in this class. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--option_data))
- `option_def` (Block List) Custom option definitions for this class. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--option_def))
- `server_hostname` (String) Server hostname for network booting (`sname` field in DHCP packet).
- `template_test` (String) Expression whose result names a subclass the client is assigned to, making this class a template class. Removing it replaces the class, since Kea does not turn a template class back into a regular class. Conflicts with `test`.
- `test` (String) Expression that a client must match to belong to this class. Kea rejects an update that changes whether the class depends on the `KNOWN` or `UNKNOWN` built-in classes. Conflicts with `template_test`.
- `user_context` (String) Arbitrary JSON data stored with this client class.
- `valid_lifetime` (Number) Lease lifetime in seconds for clients in this class.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Unique identifier for the client class, equal to its name.

<a id="nestedblock--option_data"></a>
### Nested Schema for `option_data`

Optional:

- `always_send` (Boolean) Always send this option, even if not requested by the client.
- `client_classes` (Set of String) Only send this option to clients in these classes. Requires Kea 3.1.0 or newer.
- `code` (Number) Option code (0-255). Required if `name` is not set.
- `csv_format` (Boolean) When `true` (default), data is comma-separated values. When `false`, data is raw bytes as hex (`dead` or `0xdead`), colon/space-delimited octets (`de:ad` or `de ad`), or a quoted string (`'text'`).
- `data` (String) Option value. Format depends on `csv_format`.
- `name` (String) Option name (e.g., `domain-name-servers`). Required if `code` is not set.
- `never_send` (Boolean) Never send this option to the client.
- `space` (String) Option space. Defaults to `dhcp4`.


<a id="nestedblock--option_def"></a>
### Nested Schema for `option_def`

Required:

- `code` (Number) Option code (0-255).
- `name` (String) Option name.
- `type` (String) Option data type (e.g., `uint8`, `string`, `ipv4-address`, `record`).

Optional:

- `array` (Boolean) Whether the option carries an array of values of `type`. Defaults to `false`.
- `encapsulate` (String) Option space encapsulated by this option.
- `record_types` (String) Comma-separated field types when `type` is `record`.
- `space` (String) Option space. Defaults to `dhcp4`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Client classes are imported by name
terraform import kea_dhcp4_client_class.voip voip-phones
```
